lead: A spacecraft runs its own power station, its own thermal control and its own pointing system, with no pilot and no maintenance visit. The solar array must make electricity in sunlight, the battery must carry the load through eclipse, heat can leave only by radiation, and the payload must be pointed to within arcseconds. Only a few universities teach this inside an avionics unit; space-systems courses treat it as core material.
prereq: You need Unit 3 for power generation and batteries, and Unit 4 for spacecraft avionics architecture.

sections.h3: Electrical power: make it, store it, regulate it

blocks.text: The power system has three blocks: the solar array, the battery, and the power conditioning and distribution unit (PCDU). The array makes direct current while the Sun is visible. The battery carries the whole load during eclipse. The PCDU converts, regulates and switches that power out to every load on the bus.

Two regulation schemes are common. A shunt regulator dumps surplus array current into a resistor or a switch when the battery is full; it is simple and cheap. Maximum power point tracking (MPPT) moves the array's operating voltage so it stays on its peak power curve as temperature and illumination change; it extracts more energy but costs more mass and money.
A regulated bus holds a fixed voltage such as 28 V or 50 V, so payloads see a clean supply. An unregulated bus follows the battery voltage and is lighter, but every load must tolerate the swing.
E_ecl = P_load × t_ecl ÷ 60      C = E_ecl ÷ (DoD × η_dis)      P_arr = (P_load + E_ecl × 60 ÷ t_sun) ÷ η_arr
blocks.where: E_ecl is the eclipse energy in Wh; P_load is the payload plus bus load in W; t_ecl is the eclipse time in minutes; C is the battery capacity in Wh; DoD is the allowed depth of discharge (0 to 1); η_dis is the discharge efficiency; t_sun is the sunlight time in minutes; η_arr is the array and harness efficiency; P_arr is the array output at beginning of life in W.

items: Energy out in eclipse = load power × eclipse time.
Battery capacity = eclipse energy ÷ (depth of discharge × discharge efficiency).
Recharge power = eclipse energy ÷ sunlight time.
Array output = (load power + recharge power) ÷ array efficiency.

sections.h3: Thermal control: dumping heat by radiation

blocks.text: There is no air in space, so a spacecraft loses heat by radiation only. A radiator of area A at absolute temperature T dumps heat at the rate given by the Stefan-Boltzmann law.

blocks.where: Q is the heat dumped in W; ε is the emissivity, a number between 0 and 1; σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/(m²·K⁴) is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant; A is the radiating area in m²; T is the absolute temperature in K.

blocks.text: Multi-layer insulation (MLI) is a blanket of many thin aluminised sheets. It blocks radiation and conduction together and keeps a box warm with almost no heater power. Radiators are coated white or fitted with optical solar reflectors so their emissivity stays high while they absorb little sunlight.

Passive control uses MLI, surface coatings, radiators and heat pipes — sealed tubes that carry heat from a hot box to a radiator by evaporating a fluid at the hot end. Active control adds heaters, louvers and pumped loops. A 200 W box at 300 K with ε = 0.9 needs A = 200 ÷ (0.9 × 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ × 300⁴) = 0.48 m².

Spin stabilisation spins the whole craft about its axis of largest moment of inertia. Like a top it resists disturbance and needs no wheels, but the payload sweeps round with the spin, so it suits simple spin-stabilised satellites. Three-axis control holds the body fixed in inertial space.

items: Reaction wheel: a disc whose speed is changed by a motor. The craft turns the other way to conserve angular momentum, using no propellant.
Momentum wheel: runs at a constant bias speed and gives gyroscopic stiffness.
Control moment gyro (CMG): a gimballed spinning wheel, so a small wheel makes a large torque.
Thruster: fires gas for big slews and for unloading wheels, at the cost of propellant.
Magnetorquer: a coil that pushes against the Earth's magnetic field, a small torque in low Earth orbit only.

blocks.text: Sensors are the sun sensor (coarse, two-axis), the star tracker (arcsecond class), the Earth sensor (infrared horizon) and the gyro (rate, short term). Disturbance torques come from gravity gradient, solar radiation pressure, residual atmosphere and the magnetic field.

blocks.where: τ is the commanded control torque in N·m; θ is the attitude error in rad; θ̇ is the rate error in rad/s; K_p is the proportional gain in N·m/rad; K_d is the derivative gain in N·m·s/rad. The derivative term adds damping so the craft does not oscillate.

blocks.text: A wheel absorbs disturbance momentum over time and its speed keeps rising until it saturates. Thrusters or magnetorquers then dump that stored momentum; this is desaturation.

figure.caption: The bus laid out from payload down to structure. Power, thermal and attitude control are the three subsystems that keep the payload alive and pointed.

examples.question: A satellite carries a 500 W payload in a 96 min orbit with a 35 min eclipse. The battery may be taken to 90% depth of discharge at 90% discharge efficiency. The array works for the remaining 61 min and 10% of its output is lost in the array and harness. Find the battery capacity and the array output at beginning of life.
steps: Eclipse energy E_ecl = P_load × t_ecl ÷ 60 = 500 × 35 ÷ 60 = 291.67 Wh.
Array must supply load plus recharge = 500 + 286.89 = 786.89 W.
examples.answer: Battery capacity 360.08 Wh (about 360 Wh) and array output 874.32 W (about 875 W) at beginning of life.
examples.check:
P = 500.0
t_orb = 96.0
t_ecl = 35.0
dod = 0.9
eta_dis = 0.9
eta_arr = 0.9
t_sun = t_orb - t_ecl
E = P * t_ecl / 60.0
C = E / (dod * eta_dis)
P_rec = E / (t_sun / 60.0)
P_arr = (P + P_rec) / eta_arr
print(round(E, 2))
print(round(C, 2))
print(round(P_rec, 2))
print(round(P_arr, 2))

traps: Sizing the array for the payload alone and forgetting the recharge energy; the array must also refill the battery.
Using the full 96 min orbit period instead of the 35 min eclipse when sizing the battery, which triples the capacity.
Putting degrees Celsius into εσAT⁴; the Stefan-Boltzmann law needs kelvin, and a Celsius value can give a negative or wildly wrong area.
Multiplying by depth of discharge and efficiency instead of dividing; capacity is always larger than the eclipse energy.
Assuming reaction wheels alone can hold attitude for years; disturbance torques saturate them and they must be desaturated.

quiz.q: Name the three blocks of a spacecraft power system.
quiz.a: Solar array, battery, and power conditioning and distribution unit (PCDU).

quiz.q: Why does a spacecraft need a battery if it has a solar array?
quiz.a: During eclipse the array produces nothing, so the battery must carry the full load; the array recharges it in sunlight.

quiz.q: A 300 W payload has a 40 min eclipse in a 100 min orbit. Depth of discharge 0.8, discharge efficiency 0.95. Find the battery capacity.
A radiator must dump 150 W at 320 K with emissivity 0.85. Find its area.
Why must reaction wheels be desaturated, and what is used to do it?
quiz.a: Disturbance torques slowly raise wheel speed until the wheel reaches its limit and can give no more torque. Thrusters or magnetorquers then dump the stored momentum, bringing wheel speed back to its bias value.

quiz.q: A spin-stabilised satellite is simple yet a three-axis satellite is used for a camera payload. Why?
quiz.a: A spinning craft sweeps its payload round once per spin, so the camera cannot stare at a target. Three-axis control holds the body fixed, so the payload keeps its pointing for the whole pass, at the cost of wheels, sensors and a control law.

beyond: Not for the exam. Flight practice mixes these blocks: the PCDU, the thermal loops and the attitude electronics are usually separate units tied through a data bus, and the flight software runs a fault-detection layer above all three. Newer work looks at electric propulsion for orbit raising so the power system, not the chemical tank, sets the mass budget, and at deployable radiators for high-power payloads. Search next for eclipse energy balance, MPPT versus shunt regulation, and momentum dumping with magnetorquers.
